name: South Asian oral rehydration studies
description: Clinical studies in South Asia published in 1968 demonstrated the potential of glucose-electrolyte solutions in managing severe diarrhoeal fluid losses, including solutions consumed orally.

impact.note: Showed that drinking a glucose-salt solution can replace drips for severe diarrhoea, later used across poorer countries on several continents.

date.label: 1968 CE
date.basis: The cited historical review identifies clinical studies published in 1968.

events.statement: Clinical studies in South Asia published in 1968 demonstrated the potential of glucose-electrolyte solutions in managing severe diarrhoeal fluid losses, including solutions consumed orally.
events.caveats: This broad publication event is not a claim that all trials used oral administration or that this was the first use of oral fluids; individual primary trials need examination.

evidence.supports: Review reports 1968 studies in India and then Pakistan using glucose-containing fluid either orally or by intestinal infusion.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest evidence currently researched for this scoped record; not a claim of global priority. This broad publication event is not a claim that all trials used oral administration or that this was the first use of oral fluids; individual primary trials need examination.
